peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: NVDA 33.3% with 3/3 replicate support; INTC 23.3% with 3/3 replicate support; XYZ100 16.7% with 3/3 replicate support; MRVL 10.0% with 2/3 replicate support; MSFT 8.3% with 2/3 replicate support; MU 8.3% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is AMD's closest direct return comparator because AMD Instinct accelerators compete for the same data-center AI GPU budgets as NVIDIA's data-center GPUs. Both are fabless advanced-node semiconductor companies whose returns are highly sensitive to AI accelerator demand, supply constraints, and hyperscaler capex.

peers.name: Intel
peers.reason: Intel is the direct x86 CPU substitute across client and server, so it shares AMD's PC and server demand cycle, x86 pricing and share dynamics, and part of the data-center CPU budget. It is weighted below NVIDIA because AMD's most important incremental return driver is AI accelerator exposure rather than legacy CPU alone.

peers.name: Nasdaq-100
peers.reason: The primary hedge is also a peer because the Nasdaq-100 captures a major share of AMD's return exposure to mega-cap growth, semiconductors, discount-rate moves, and broad tech risk appetite. This is a dominant index exposure, not a remote high-beta analogy.

peers.name: Marvell Technology
peers.reason: Marvell Technology is a fabless data-center semiconductor peer selling custom AI silicon and networking/connectivity chips into the same hyperscaler capex cycle as AMD. It shares AMD's fabless model, leading-edge foundry dependence, and AI infrastructure demand exposure, making it a closer comparator than generic high-beta names.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is a major demand-side comparator: Azure is a large customer for AMD EPYC server CPUs and a key buyer of AI infrastructure that can use AMD Instinct accelerators. Its cloud and AI capex cycle maps directly into AMD data-center revenue rather than merely moving with generic risk-on sentiment.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: Micron is a leading memory maker whose returns track the same semiconductor capital-spending and pricing cycle that drives AMD, and memory is a key shared input cost and adjacent demand signal for AI servers. MU has very deep 24-hour perp liquidity of 59.489 USD millions.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: The Nasdaq-100 is AMD's dominant systematic index: AMD is a major constituent, so a large share of its daily return variation is explained by this growth and tech benchmark. It is the directly traded underlying index rather than a leveraged or wrapper proxy, which makes it preferable to SOXL (a 3x leveraged semiconductor wrapper) and to DRAM (a memory-specific ETF that misses AMD's CPU and GPU compute exposure). It also offers deep execution capacity at 112.11 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity, well above AMD's own 6.117 USD millions, making it practical as the generic market-risk hedge.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
